belongs_to: 4.5 Infographics: 'instead of rectangles, we could use triangles ... Here is the result' (tallest mountains drawn as coloured triangles); the text then says the taller triangles are also wider, which may mislead
description: Infographic version of the column graph, white background. Vertical axis labels (small, at the left): 1000m, 2000m, 3000m, 4000m, 5000m, 6000m, 7000m, 8000m (step 1000, no 0m label), each with a thin light-teal horizontal gridline across the whole width. Seven solid isosceles triangles (mountains) stand on one common baseline below the 1000m line, in this order from left to right, each a different colour: Everest = steel/teal blue, widest and tallest, tip a little above the 8000m line; Aconcagua = light green, tip just below the 7000m line; Denali = pale orange/sand, tip just above 6000m; Kilimanjaro = green-teal, tip just below 6000m; Elbrus = pale sky blue, tip about 5500m, narrower; Vinson Massif = red-orange, tip about 4800m, narrower; Koscuiszko = pale sage green, smallest, tip about 2300m, narrowest. Under each triangle a three-line label: mountain name / height / continent: 'Everest / 8848m / Asia'; 'Aconcagua / 6962m / S America'; 'Denali / 6194m / North America' (continent on two lines); 'Kilimanjaro / 5895m / Africa'; 'Elbrus / 5642m / Europe'; 'Vinson Massif / 4892m / Antarctica'; 'Koscuiszko / 2228m / Australia'.
